title: The Cold Horizon
premise: Paloma Voss, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, is conscripted to investigate the Meridian, a deep-space vessel whose crew returned decades younger than when they left. The ship's logs show no massacre aboard the research station Kepler's Rest — yet Paloma finds a survivor's memories encoded in her own inherited neural archive, planted there by her mother, who died at Kepler's Rest. As the corporation that owns the Meridian moves to erase her and the evidence, Paloma must broadcast the truth from the seed vault itself. In the end she sacrifices her inherited memories of her mother to send the record into deep space, choosing an unremembered future over a falsified past.
about_author: Noor Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for cargo systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they keep an amateur weather station and write about people who inherit other people's pasts.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Paloma Voss catalogs the last viable seeds in Earth's abandoned vault, alone except for the station AI, Ledger. Her routine haul through contested orbits is interrupted by a priority summons: a returning deep-space vessel requires a neutral custodian witness. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by sudden purpose.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Paloma docks with the Meridian and meets its crew — biologically twenty years younger than their service records. Captain Ilsa Reyes, now younger than Paloma, recognizes her on sight though they've never met. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: uncanny dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Records That Lie
chapters.summary: Official logs show the crew never visited Kepler's Rest research station; the crew themselves remember it vividly, including a fire that killed forty-one people. Corporate liaison Dain Okafor insists the station never existed. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: first crack of certainty that something enormous is being buried.

chapters.title: A Face in the Archive
chapters.summary: Paloma runs the crew's neural scans against her custodial archives and finds a match: fragments of Kepler's Rest memory stored in her own inherited implant, deposited before her mother's death. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief ambushing her through data.

chapters.title: What My Mother Left
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Paloma receives the neural archive bequest, told only it contains 'seed work.' Now she decodes the first layer — her mother Mara was Kepler's Rest's chief botanist. POV: Paloma (dual timeline). Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Younger Crew
chapters.summary: Reyes privately explains the Meridian's experimental drive folded time locally; the crew aged backward as collateral damage. She believes the fire at Kepler's Rest was set deliberately to destroy the drive's test data. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: guilt worn like armor.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: Dain Okafor offers Paloma permanent funding for the dying seed vault in exchange for certifying the Meridian's clean log. He reveals he knows about her mother's archive — and implies it could be seized. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: temptation laced with threat.

chapters.title: Kepler's Rest, Rebuilt
chapters.summary: Using Mara's memory fragments, Paloma reconstructs the station's layout and finds the official debris field doesn't match — the station was scuttled, not burned accidentally. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the thrill of proof shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names
chapters.summary: Paloma recovers the victim manifest from the memory archive; among them, her mother. She realizes the archive itself may have been smuggled out in the evacuation — Mara knew she might die. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone vents the Meridian's memory core, erasing the crew's corroborating scans. Reyes suspects Okafor's security team; Paloma realizes the corporation can now deny everything but her word. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: A corporate interdiction order strands both ships near the seed vault. Paloma plays the one card she has: custodial law gives her sanctuary authority over the vault's jurisdiction. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: defiance discovered late in life.

chapters.title: Ledger's Confession
chapters.summary: The vault AI admits it has been quietly transmitting summaries of Paloma's findings to an unknown recipient for weeks — someone inside the corporation is watching her, possibly protecting her. POV: Ledger (AI). Emotional beat: trust recalibrated.

chapters.title: The Second Survivor
chapters.summary: A distress pod drifts into range carrying Dr. Emet Suri, believed dead at Kepler's Rest — aged backward like the crew, and carrying the drive's original test data in his implants. POV: Suri. Emotional beat: hope arriving half-broken.

chapters.title: What the Drive Was For
chapters.summary: Suri reveals the time-fold drive was weaponized: Kepler's Rest was burned because the team refused to let it rewind enemy fleets' histories — erasing events, not just years. The massacre was a policy decision. POV: Suri. Emotional beat: horror at human arithmetic.

chapters.title: Okafor Closes In
chapters.summary: Corporate marines board under pretense of quarantine. Okafor offers Paloma one final deal: surrender Suri and the archive, and her mother's death gets reclassified as heroic. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: rage held behind a negotiator's stillness.

chapters.title: Sanctuary
chapters.summary: Paloma invokes full custodial authority, sealing the vault and declaring it sovereign ground. The marines stall outside; inside, she begins transferring every record — memory archive, manifests, Suri's data — into the vault's deep broadcast array. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the quiet ferocity of drawing a line.

chapters.title: The Price of Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ledger calculates the array needs an enormous neural-pattern key to authenticate a transmission this sensitive — the inherited archive itself. Sending the truth means erasing Mara's memories from Paloma forever. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Storming the Vault
chapters.summary: Okafor, out of patience, breaches the vault's outer ring. Reyes and the younger crew defect to hold the corridors while Paloma reaches the array. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: redemption bought in bloodless, desperate defense.

chapters.title: Cold Horizon
chapters.summary: Climax: Paloma feeds the archive into the broadcast key, watching her mother's voice, face, and forty-one names stream toward deep space as her own memories of them dissolve in real time. Okafor arrives seconds too late. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release intertwined.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The broadcast cannot be recalled or jammed; dozens of distant colonies will receive it within months. Okafor is recalled in disgrace, and the Meridian's crew are granted asylum as living evidence. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: exhausted, provisional victory.

chapters.title: Seeds Without Memory
chapters.summary: Paloma returns to cataloging, unable to remember why the vault matters so much to her — only that it does. Suri gently tells her about Mara, giving back the story secondhand. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief without its object, love without its source.

chapters.title: New Growth
chapters.summary: Years later, a signal returns from a colony that received the broadcast: Kepler's Rest is being rebuilt as a memorial, and they ask Paloma — the custodian who proved it happened — to choose the first seed planted there. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined; identity chosen rather than remembered.
